excerpt: Section 2.1.1, Description of PageRank Calculation (paraphrased for practice). Suppose pages T1...Tn point to page A. The parameter d is a damping factor between 0 and 1, usually set to 0.85. C(A) is the number of links going out of page A. The PageRank of A is PR(A) = (1 − d) + d (PR(T1)/C(T1) + ... + PR(Tn)/C(Tn)). The text also states that PageRanks form a probability distribution over web pages, so the sum of all pages' PageRanks will be one. PageRank can be calculated with a simple iterative algorithm and corresponds to the principal eigenvector of the normalized link matrix. It models a 'random surfer' who keeps clicking links at random and occasionally gets bored and jumps to a random page; d is the probability that the surfer keeps clicking.
focus: Explain the PageRank formula of Section 2.1.1 on a small directed graph of 3 to 6 pages given as an editable 0/1 link matrix. Let the learner change d, the links and the number of iterations; show the graph with node sizes proportional to PageRank, the per-iteration values and convergence. Guide them through (a) d = 0, where every page gets 1 − d, and (b) a page with many incoming links. Make clear that the formula as printed gives values summing to the number of pages N (when every page has outgoing links), not to one, and state how pages without outgoing links are handled. Check that the fixed point satisfies the formula, that values sum to N without dangling pages, and that d = 0 gives PR = 1 for every page.
audience: Second-year engineering undergraduates who know matrices and basic probability.
